subject: general
question: Which of the following is a mineral-based industry that uses ore or other minerals as raw materials?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Iron and steel**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Iron and steel industry** is classified as a mineral-based industry since it uses iron ore, a mineral, as its primary raw material.
 
• Iron and steel are essential materials for industrial development and are used in infrastructure, manufacturing, and construction activities.
 
• The iron and steel industry is often considered the backbone of industrialization due to its role in producing machinery, transportation vehicles, and buildings.
 
• India is one of the largest producers of steel globally, with major steel plants located in cities like Jamshedpur, Bhilai, and Rourkela.
 
• The industry also contributes significantly to employment generation and GDP growth in mineral-rich regions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mineral-Based Industries:**

 
 
• These industries depend on minerals as their primary raw materials for production.
 
• Examples include iron and steel, cement, aluminum, and petrochemical industries.
 
 
 
• **Iron Ore:**
 
 
• It is a naturally occurring mineral used to extract iron for industrial applications.
 
• India's major iron ore reserves are found in Odisha, Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh, Karnataka, and Goa.
 
 
 
• **Steel Production Process:**
 
 
• Involves several stages, including mining, smelting, refining, and rolling.
 
• Modern techniques include Blast Furnace and Electric Arc Furnace methods.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Steel:**
 
 
• Steel is vital for infrastructure development, such as bridges, railways, and airports.
 
• It is also used in the automotive, defense, and energy sectors.
